land.text: Abydos and Thinis, the page says after the fall of the 13th Dynasty

predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Thirteenth and Fourteenth Dynasties as predecessors.

successors.note: Infobox "succeeded by the Seventeenth Dynasty"; the page does not say how the dynasty ended.

capitals.name: Abydos
capitals.note: Infobox "Capital: Abydos"; the seat was probably Abydos or Thinis, a few miles to the north.

correction.text: parts of Middle and Upper Egypt around Abydos or Thinis, south to Hu about 50 km away

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; no Cliopatria row. The page says the dynasty is hypothesised to have ruled "parts of Middle and Upper Egypt", with a southern limit probably at Hu and a graffito that may reach north to Beni Hasan (uncertain). A 60 km radius around Abydos is the researcher's core reading; the Beni Hasan claim is not drawn. No area figure.

ledger.note: 1650: the Abydos Dynasty is hypothesised to arise at Abydos after the fall of the 13th Dynasty. The infobox gives c. 1650–1600 ("from approximately 1650 to 1600 BC"); the Second Intermediate Period page gives c. 1640–1620 and "Abydos or Thinis". The existence of the dynasty is itself hypothetical (Senebkay's tomb, found in 2014, may confirm it).

1600: the Abydos Dynasty ends (c. 1600 in the infobox). The Second Intermediate Period page says it ended when the Hyksos expanded into Upper Egypt; the dynasty's own page does not describe the end. The Seventeenth Dynasty of Thebes follows. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Counterpart hyksos added: the Second Intermediate Period page says 'The Abydos Dynasty ceased when the Hyksos expanded into Upper Egypt.'

certainty.note: Only a hypothesised southern limit at Hu is given.

sources.title: Second Intermediate Period of Egypt
sources.note: c. 1640–1620 and the Hyksos expansion into Upper Egypt.

notes: A hypothesised dynasty (the page: Ilin-Tomich suggests Senebkay "might be a king of the Theban 16th Dynasty"; Marée doubts one workshop served two enemy dynasties). Four kings are attributed (Wepwawetemsaf, Pantjeny, Snaaib, Senebkay) but the page assigns no reign lengths and some may belong to the 13th or 16th Dynasty, so no ruler strip. Dates: infobox 1650–1600, Second Intermediate Period page 1640–1620. The Abydos shape touches the Theban 16th Dynasty at Hu (that dynasty reached "at least as far north as Hu" on the Second Intermediate Period page). me-03-b's Seventeenth Dynasty dossier lists this as predecessor.
